patch.value: update-many ignores an unknown flat update key where a single update refuses it by name

Observed while fixing typed null handling in update-many. runAction('update-many', { options: { ids: [id], bogus: 'x', description: 'changed' } }) changes the description and reports one updated row; the unknown key is dropped without a warning. The same payload through runAction('update') refuses with: Unknown update option "bogus". Did you mean "body"? No changes were made. The GH-1520 admission check covers native create and update only, so a misspelled bulk field (for example asignee) is silently not applied to any matched row.

runAction update-many refuses an undeclared flat update key by name with the nearest declared key before any row changes, in the flat and nested spellings; Declared aliases, runtime schema fields and extension fields stay accepted; MCP update-many keeps its transport contract; A spec proves parity with the single update refusal for the same key
An unknown update key in an update-many payload is refused by name, as a single update refuses it
The unknown key is dropped and the remaining fields are applied to every matched row
